item.text: {"question_id":"5B.10","answer":"The evidence does not demonstrate that Tshisekedi left a stronger and more durable economic trajectory by the end of 2023. There is material evidence of ruler-period government action: the administration adopted medium-term fiscal planning and risk-management rules, formal audit and budget-transparency controls, and a World Bank-supported economic-governance reform program covering treasury, procurement, revenue mobilization, extractive-sector oversight, and utility appointments (BATCH-0029-E003; BATCH-0029-E005; BATCH-0014-E002). The government also continued the flagship PDL-145T; officials reported more than 300–400 works ready by August 2023, but the report is government-produced and does not establish completed-service quality, equitable incidence, or budget execution (BATCH-0019-E009; BATCH-0010-E004). The free-primary-education enrollment increase is associated with a policy implemented since 2019, includes 2021–2022 outcomes, and had World Bank support; it therefore cannot by itself establish a 2023 or Tshisekedi-exclusive trajectory effect (BATCH-0014-E004). The 2023 Sicomines renegotiation indicates a possible corrective response, but the underlying failures predated 2023 and the reported improved agreement outcome occurred in January 2024, outside the period (BATCH-0011-E007). Against these partial and attribution-qualified positives, tenure-level reporting indicates the Congolese franc fell from about 1,600 to almost 2,700 per dollar, high crisis or emergency food insecurity nearly doubled to nearly 26 million, and more than 60 percent of the population lived below $2.15 per day; these outcomes are not solely attributable to the ruler and are confounded by inherited poverty, conflict, and external conditions, but they weigh against a demonstrated broad improvement (BATCH-0028-E020). In 2023, inflation was reported at 33.9 percent at year-end and 23.33 percent on average, while fiscal execution was mixed: revenues reached 91.22 percent of forecast, general-budget execution 87.38 percent, and expenditure 96.49 percent (BATCH-0022-E008). More than 25 million people faced crisis or emergency food insecurity amid conflict and insufficient rural-development investment, and displacement reached 6.8–6.9 million by late 2023 (BATCH-0020-E009; BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0013-E014). The World Bank concluded that growth under the existing macroeconomic framework would not translate into improved living conditions without ambitious reforms, while its climate assessment identified continuing needs for stronger institutions, resilient infrastructure, food security, energy access, poverty reduction, and social inclusion (BATCH-0016-E013; BATCH-0013-E001). Persistent implementation and fairness concerns further limit the durability claim: parliamentarians citing the Court of Accounts reported excessive overruns, uncertified-debt payments, and works listed without observed field action; the State Department reported ineffective anti-corruption enforcement, opaque special accounts, alleged phantom payments, and official complicity in illicit mineral trade; and Amnesty documented forced evictions, inadequate compensation, and absent remedies around mining projects, although none of these sources establishes Tshisekedi's personal direction (BATCH-0024-E004; BATCH-0011-E013; BATCH-0010-E018). Accordingly, the record supports partial institutional and policy progress under his administration, but not a demonstrated stronger, fairer, and durable inherited-to-left economic trajectory within the 2019–2023 period or by the end of 2023.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0014-E002","BATCH-0019-E009","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0011-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E020","BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0016-E013","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0011-E013","BATCH-0010-E018"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence provides a consistent baseline-to-2023 series for household income, employment, inequality, productivity, or investment tied to Tshisekedi-attributed decisions.","Several positive measures are formal rules, partner-supported reforms, government-reported outputs, or lagged outcomes; execution quality, distribution, and durable effects remain insufficiently established.","Negative outcomes are substantially confounded by inherited poverty, armed conflict, commodity and global conditions, donor involvement, and other institutional actors; they cannot be treated as solely presidential effects.","The supplied evidence does not establish the ruler's personal direction of the cited budget, corruption, mining, or macroeconomic outcomes. Synthesis is limited to the administration and ruler-period context.","The evidence is concentrated in 2023 and a 2019–2023 tenure comparison, so longer-run post-2023 durability cannot be assessed. "],"corrections_made":["Removed the human-rights decline as positive economic-trajectory evidence; BATCH-0025-E009 is not an economic outcome and was excluded.","Reclassified education, PDL-145T, governance reforms, fiscal rules, and Sicomines renegotiation as partial or attribution-qualified evidence rather than demonstrated durable economic improvement.","Added the tenure-level currency, food-insecurity, poverty, and displacement evidence from BATCH-0028-E020.","Added the World Bank finding that growth was not translating into improved living conditions without ambitious reforms.","Separated formal rules and reported implementation from independently demonstrated outcomes, distributional effects, and durable trajectory.","Preserved external conditions, institutional constraints, implementation lags, partner support, and limits on personal attribution."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A fuller household-welfare, inequality, employment, productivity, investment, and regional-distribution series could materially refine the trajectory judgment.","Independent verification of PDL-145T completion, service quality, budget execution, and incidence could clarify whether reported outputs produced durable broad-based gains.","Evidence on the execution and effects of the governance reforms, fiscal controls, and Sicomines renegotiation could distinguish formal policy progress from durable institutional change.","A comparative baseline separating Tshisekedi-attributable outcomes from conflict, commodity, donor, predecessor, and global effects would improve causal calibration."]}
